title: Phenophase‐linked management strategies for the stink bug, Tessaratoma javanica (Thunberg) (Hemiptera: Tessaratomidae) in litchi in the Eastern Plateau and Hill regions of India
content:
The study focused on phenophase-linked management of the litchi stink bug (Tessaratoma javanica), a major pest that causes severe flower and fruit drop in litchi, leading to yield losses of up to 90%. Field experiments conducted during 2022–2023 in Shahi variety orchards at Ranchi evaluated 10 insecticidal and biopesticidal treatments applied across three critical crop phenophases based on the BBCH scale: inflorescence emergence (500–503), end of flowering (619–621), and fruit development (702–703). In addition to chemical and biopesticide sprays, a mechanical “stink bug barrier band” made of red polythene and grease was introduced to restrict nymph migration. The treatments were assessed for their efficacy in suppressing pest populations (nymphs and adults), their effects on egg parasitism by natural enemies, and their impact on pollinator foraging behaviour. Results revealed that some treatments were highly effective against T. javanica, while the barrier band significantly reduced nymph migration. Selective treatments were also found to be safer for parasitoids and pollinators. Overall, the integration of phenophase-specific insecticide applications with mechanical barriers provides an effective, pollinator-safe, and eco-friendly strategy for the sustainable management of T. javanica in litchi orchards.


Abstract

The litchi stink bug, Tessaratoma javanica, is a major sucking insect pest of litchi that causes damage to litchi flowers and fruits in India. Chemical insecticide-based management strategies negatively impact insect pollinators, as litchi is a highly cross-pollinated entomophilous crop, and are potentially detrimental to egg parasitoids of litchi stink bugs. Therefore, sustainable and environmentally friendly solutions that effectively suppress stink bugs while conserving parasitoids and pollinators are needed. The efficacy of different groups of insecticides and their combination with a mechanical barrier (stinkBug barrier band) was examined at different phenophases, and their safety for pollinators and natural enemies in litchi orchards was assessed. The results revealed that various insecticides and their combinations showed different levels of efficacy against litchi stink bugs. The insecticide mixture of profenophos 50% EC (1.5 mL/L) + thiacloprid 21.7% SC (0.5 mL/L) proved effective against litchi stink bugs and was relatively safer for the honey bees, as assessed in terms of foraging rate and speed during full flowering and egg parasitoids at the end of flowering of litchi. The mixture of thiacloprid 21.7% SC (0.5 mL/L) + lambda cyhalothrin 5% EC (1.0 mL/L) with the stinkBug barrier band on tree trunks at the fruit development stage was most effective. Based on the results of the present study, profenophos 50% EC + thiacloprid 21.7% SC at the end of flowering and thiacloprid 21.7% SC + lambda cyhalothrin 5% EC with stinkBug barrier bands on tree trunks at the fruit development stage are recommended for managing the litchi stink bug, T. javanica in the litchi ecosystem.
